title: Why drums did not record in the early days
summary: Early recordings only picked up cymbal and wood blocks, not snare or bass drum.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Wonderful drum band, I think. Well, in those days, you see, the drums wouldn't record, they didn't use drums. Oh, no. No. The only thing that would record in those days was the cymbal. You couldn't hear a drum or a bass drum like you can now. No, it's funny.
So on those records he had just the cymbal on the wood band?
Just the cymbal on the wood blocks. Just the cymbal on the wood blocks. Or a block, yeah. Yeah. The bass drum, snare drum wouldn't record. I couldn't understand that. Oh, I didn't see.
They can pick up if you stamp your foot? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Well, I guess that's a better word question. You got any quick questions, Richie?
